title: From Entanglement Bootstrap to DHR Theory
abstract: We establish a direct connection between the entanglement bootstrap and the Doplicher--Haag--Roberts theory of superselection sectors for two-dimensional quantum spin systems. Under the entanglement-bootstrap assumptions, we prove Haag duality and establish a one-to-one correspondence between simple entanglement-bootstrap anyon types and irreducible superselection sectors. For each fusion channel, we further construct an affine bijection from density matrices on the entanglement-bootstrap fusion space to normalized positive intertwiners in the corresponding operator-algebraic fusion channel. These results connect the entropic and operator-algebraic descriptions of anyons directly, without passing through exactly solvable lattice models.
summary: This paper bridges two advanced theoretical frameworks—the entanglement bootstrap and DHR theory—to provide a unified understanding of topological order in 2D quantum spin systems. It establishes a direct, non-model-dependent correspondence between the topological charges (anyons) derived from entanglement entropy and the superselection sectors of the underlying quantum field theory. This is a major theoretical advance in characterizing quantum phases of matter.
main_problem: The paper establishes a rigorous mathematical connection between the entanglement bootstrap approach and the Doplicher–Haag–Roberts (DHR) theory for characterizing topological order in 2D quantum spin systems.
main_result: It proves that simple entanglement-bootstrap anyon types correspond one-to-one with irreducible superselection sectors, and constructs an affine bijection between density matrices on the entanglement fusion space and positive intertwiners in the operator algebra fusion channel.
method: The authors employ advanced concepts from algebraic quantum field theory, combining entropy considerations (entanglement bootstrap) with the structure of local observable algebras (DHR theory).
model_or_system: The theory applies to two-dimensional gapped topological phases, specifically quantum spin systems defined on a lattice structure. The analysis uses local algebras associated with finite lattice regions.
key_observables: Von Neumann entropy, mutual information, entanglement measures, anyon types, and superselection sectors.
important_parameters: The analysis depends on the geometry of the lattice regions (e.g., hexagonal tiling) and the assumption of a fixed pure reference state $\omega$.
main_assumptions: The core assumptions are the 'entanglement-bootstrap assumptions,' which allow for the derivation of structural properties like Haag duality without relying on exactly solvable lattice models.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate local configurations for the axioms defining the theory and show the geometric relationship between different regions (e.g., $\Omega$ and its thickening $\Omega^+$).
paper_structure: The paper builds logically by first setting up the entanglement bootstrap, proving structural theorems like Haag duality, recalling the DHR framework, establishing the correspondence between the two formalisms, and finally developing detailed fusion space relations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, purely mathematical framework to characterize topological order using entanglement entropy, linking it directly to the rigorous algebraic structure of local observables, which is fundamental to understanding quantum phases.
